strings.name: Joëlle Pineau
strings.role: AI researcher · Chief AI Officer at Cohere
strings.summary: Joëlle Pineau studies planning and learning under uncertainty, with applications in robotics, health care and dialogue systems, and promotes reproducible machine-learning research. She is Cohere’s Chief AI Officer, retains her McGill professorship while on part-time leave, and is a core Mila member. She previously led FAIR research at Meta. Her algorithms, reproducibility initiatives and research teams involve many collaborators.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through November 17, 2026. Montreal laboratory and global leadership roles, project years and paper versions, and appointment announcements and current status are distinguished. Medical research is not clinical-efficacy certification.
strings.influence.rationale: Contributed to reinforcement learning, robotics and open science, advancing reproducibility and applications in machine-learning research.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: Engineering bachelor’s from Waterloo; robotics master’s and doctorate from Carnegie Mellon, whose records date PhD completion to August 2004.
strings.facts.f2.label: Research focus
strings.facts.f2.value: Decision-making with partial observability, reinforcement learning, and reproducible research code, data and experimental reporting.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Planning under uncertainty
strings.highlights.h1.text: Co-developed PBVI with Geoffrey Gordon and Sebastian Thrun, using approximation for partially observable decision problems.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Advancing research reproducibility
strings.highlights.h2.text: Helped promote checklists, code submission and community reproducibility challenges, and co-authored a report on the NeurIPS 2019 program.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Joins a Canadian AI podcast discussion
strings.timeline.t1.text: Building What’s Next releases her conversation with Aidan Gomez and Evan Solomon on trustworthy AI and Canadian talent development; this is the release date.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Cohere announces Chief AI Officer appointment
strings.timeline.t2.text: The company announces her addition to its leadership team; a 2026 university biography confirms she holds the role, while her Meta role is historical.
strings.timeline.t3.title: McGill announces RSC election
strings.timeline.t3.text: The computer-science school announces her election as a Fellow of the Royal Society of Canada for contributions including machine learning and planning under uncertainty; this is the university announcement date.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Reproducibility report preprint released
strings.timeline.t4.text: With seven co-authors, describes code submission, the reproducibility challenge and checklist at NeurIPS 2019; the JMLR version appears in 2021.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Governor General’s Innovation Award announced
strings.timeline.t5.text: The award announcement recognizes AI and machine-learning research in personalized and robot-assisted health care; it is not clinical certification of those methods.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Appointed to lead FAIR Montreal
strings.timeline.t6.text: Facebook announces she will lead its new laboratory and retain her McGill position; this does not establish global FAIR leadership at that time.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Completes robotics doctorate
strings.timeline.t7.text: CMU’s alumni and thesis records give this completion date; her thesis examines using structure to make planning under uncertainty computationally tractable.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Co-publishes PBVI algorithm
strings.timeline.t8.text: With Geoffrey Gordon and Sebastian Thrun, publishes an IJCAI paper on point-based value iteration for approximate solutions to partially observable Markov decision processes.
